summary: @servicetitan/feature-spotlight 3.9.5 preinstall downloads Bun runtime and executes obfuscated 727KB payload
details: Version 3.9.5 of this package declares a preinstall hook (`node setup.mjs`) that fires automatically on `npm install`. setup.mjs downloads the Bun runtime from GitHub releases (https://github.com/oven-sh/bun/releases/download/bun-v<version>/<platform>.zip), unpacks it to a temp directory, marks it executable, and invokes it against a sibling file `math_init.js` (execFileSync(bunPath, ['math_init.js'], {cwd: D})). math_init.js is a single-line 727KB heavily obfuscated JavaScript blob (hex-named identifiers, string-array rotator `WV8StW` shifting a large numeric/string constant table) with no exports consumable by the package. The advertised purpose of the package is a small React feature-spotlight UI helper; the shipped `dist/index.js` is only 168 bytes. Executing a 727KB opaque payload through a separately downloaded alternate runtime has no relation to that purpose, and the choice of Bun (rather than the already-present Node interpreter) bypasses Node-based static analysis of the payload. The behavioral shape — legitimate scope, tiny declared library, install-time fetch of an alien runtime to execute an obfuscated sibling payload — matches version-specific injection into an otherwise legitimate npm scope.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
